title: Why Cities Run Out of Water
paras: For most of the twentieth century, city planners {{assumed|assume}} that fresh water would always be {{available}} when people turned on the tap. That assumption is now being questioned. When researchers {{analysed|analyse}} {{data}} from more than two hundred large cities, they {{estimated|estimate}} that one in four already faces regular water shortages.

It is {{evident}} that climate is only one {{factor}}. Population growth, ageing pipes and poor planning also play a part. In many places, water is not {{distributed|distribute}} fairly: wealthy suburbs receive a steady supply, while poorer districts depend on trucks and wells.

Local {{authorities|authority}} have tried several {{approaches|approach}}. Some have built desalination plants, which turn sea water into drinking water but use large amounts of energy. Others have invested in recycling waste water for farms and factories. Cape Town, for example, cut its consumption by almost half during a severe drought by limiting each household to fifty litres a day.

Experts argue that cities must {{assess}} the true cost of each option, including its impact on the {{environment}}. A plant that supplies water cheaply today may damage marine life for decades. The greatest {{benefit}}, many suggest, comes from simple measures: fixing leaks, charging fair prices and teaching people to value every drop.

questions.q: What did researchers find after studying data from over two hundred cities?
options: Most cities have enough water for the future
About a quarter of cities already experience regular shortages
Climate is the only cause of water shortages
Desalination is the cheapest solution
questions.why: 第一段：they estimated that one in four already faces regular water shortages（one in four = 四分之一）

questions.q: According to the passage, what is a disadvantage of desalination plants?
options: They cannot produce drinking water
They are only useful for farms
They consume a lot of energy and may harm marine life
They make water distribution unfair
questions.why: 第三段 use large amounts of energy，第四段 may damage marine life。这种需要综合两处信息的题在 PTE 单选题里很常见

questions.q: What is the main idea of the final paragraph?
options: Simple, low-cost measures may bring the greatest benefit
Cities should build more desalination plants
Water should be free for everyone
Cape Town's policy failed
questions.why: 最后一句：The greatest benefit … comes from simple measures

title: The Price of a Cup of Coffee
paras: A cup of coffee may seem simple, but the {{concept}} of its price is surprisingly complex. The final cost {{consists|consist}} of many parts: the beans, transport, roasting, rent, wages and tax. Growers, who do most of the hard work, often receive less than ten percent of what the customer pays.

To understand why, we need some historical {{context}}. Coffee was first grown as an {{export}} crop in colonies, where the {{economy}} was designed to send raw materials to Europe. Many producing countries still {{derive}} a large share of their national income from coffee, yet they have little control over its price, which is set on international markets.

Because prices change so much, farmers struggle to plan ahead or obtain {{finance}}. Some have formed cooperatives and signed long-term {{contracts|contract}} with buyers. Fair trade organisations have {{established|establish}} a minimum price that protects growers when the market falls.

However, there is no simple {{formula}} for fairness. Critics point out that it is hard to {{define}} a fair price, and that certification fees can be expensive for small farms. Still, these schemes {{constitute}} an important step. They remind consumers that every cup connects them to a long chain of people, and that the choices they make at the counter can shape lives on the other side of the world.

questions.q: Why do coffee-producing countries have little control over coffee prices?
options: Because they do not export coffee
Because prices are set on international markets
Because fair trade organisations fix the price
Because consumers refuse to pay more
questions.why: 第二段：its price, which is set on international markets

questions.q: What does the fair trade minimum price do?
options: It guarantees growers receive most of the final price
It removes certification fees
It protects growers when market prices fall
It increases the price of coffee for consumers
questions.why: 第三段：a minimum price that protects growers when the market falls

questions.q: Which statement best reflects the writer's attitude to fair trade schemes?
options: They are perfect and should be compulsory
They are useless because fees are high
They have limitations but are still a valuable step
They have made coffee too expensive
questions.why: 第四段：先说 However … no simple formula（有局限），再说 Still … an important step（仍然有价值）。PTE 常考作者态度，注意 however / still 这类转折词
